title: jf-docs-analyze
description: Understand the source analysis that establishes API facts and a library mental model.

children: establishes the evidence for documentation before pages are planned or written. It analyzes the library at the target version and does not write pages or change library source.
The stage receives the package, framework, and version from

. It starts with public package entry points, then follows source, type declarations, tests, and examples. Existing docs and comments are claims to verify. Earlier majors use source at their last release tag.
When workspace analysis exists, the agent reads its state first and re-analyzes stale packages and affected concepts. A changed target major requires fresh analysis.
Import paths, kinds, parameters, defaults, returns, errors, limitations, and related exports
Concepts, relationships, state flow, lifecycle, integrations, and prerequisites
Generic inference, overloads, narrowing, schema-derived types, and what developers see
Initialization, call order, side effects, transitions, edge cases, and integration requirements
Basic use, advanced use, and extension points

Internal symbols are not documented as supported API. Stability, deprecation, dates, release facts, and performance characteristics require evidence. Disagreements between docs, tests, and implementation are recorded rather than silently resolved by assumption.

The output identifies the target and source revision, package map, public API inventory, mental model, type and runtime behavior, workflows, gaps, and open questions. Important facts cite a source file and symbol; inferences are labeled.
In a documentation workspace, package analysis lives in
records the source revision and package status.
Use jf-docs-analyze to establish how the current package's step schemas determine field values. Record public exports, inference behavior, lifecycle requirements, and gaps before planning pages.
later checks documentation against source independently.
